metadata_used.title: Your headphones don't block sound. They add it.
metadata_used.description:
Noise cancelling has a deadline. The microphone hears the noise about 87 microseconds before your eardrum does — three centimetres of air — and in that window the headphone has to measure the wave, invert it and play it back. Land it 40 microseconds late and the cancelling starts to fail. Miss by 100 and, at 1 kHz, you're a tenth of a wave wrong. That's why an engine disappears and the person next to you doesn't.

Sources:
US 9,786,264 (feedforward time alignment) · https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9786264
SoundGuys, how active noise cancelling works · https://www.soundguys.com/how-noise-cancelling-headphones-work-12380/
PMC, measured ANC attenuation · https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9572409/
